F-540.next_action: none -- the daily credential-health cadence runs in production and refresh-token rotation is proven and persisted there
evidence: research/final_build/w4/evidence_FMBATCH1/prod_api_audit_credential_health_20261021T0242Z.json (production b931d17, read-only GET /api/audit?action=etsy.credential_health): 10 daily readings 2026-10-12..2026-10-21; from 2026-10-13T03:25Z every one is status HEALTHY, stored+openable under the current sealing key, scopes listings_d/r/w, shops_r/w, transactions_r with missing_scopes [], and a live refresh attempted+ok whose rotations_before -> rotations_after advanced (0->1 on 10-13 ... 73->74 on 10-21) with updated_at persisted; values never shown (token_fingerprint only, exposes_credentials false). 2026-10-12 read UNKNOWN (no live attempt) -- the reading before the grant, kept, not a pass
F-540.reason: Criterion: 'Continuously monitor stored/openable Etsy credential status, granted scopes, expiry and refresh health without exposing values. Refresh-token rotation must be proven in production and persisted atomically.' The matrix's missing_part ('nothing monitors it on a cadence ... rotations: 0') is stale: the cadence is deployed and production shows 9 consecutive daily HEALTHY readings with a successful live rotation each day, persisted (rotations 74, updated_at advancing), values never exposed. Atomic persistence is pinned by the race test (a rotation that lost the race is refused). test_etsy_readback_observe 37/37 and test_etsy_oauth_callback green on this branch (FMBATCH1.md).

gate.detail: the daily schema read runs in production (etsy_api OPEN); the drift consumer is on claude/w4-FMBATCH1

F-010.consumer: src/brambleloop/runtime/release.py::handle_taxonomy_refresh (daily listing.taxonomy_refresh cadence) -> halting P1 taxonomy-drift:<slug> + listing.seo re-queue; release.py::_persist_search_profile resolves it
F-010.next_action: release: deploy a build carrying claude/w4-FMBATCH1; production then diffs every new snapshot (the first property-schema read on the next release is itself such a change and re-queues the UNKNOWN Launch-0 profiles)
F-010.reason: Criterion: 'Periodically re-check category/attribute schemas for platform changes.' The re-check ran daily but nothing consumed a change. integrations/taxonomy_drift.py diffs each new snapshot against its predecessor (nodes removed/added/moved/renamed, per-node property changes, a node gaining a child), opens a halting P1 for each product whose CHOSEN node changed, re-queues its listing.seo once per snapshot, and resolves when the profile is rebuilt on the new snapshot; UNKNOWN profiles are re-queued without an incident. 9/9 tests; disabling the hook fails the 3 runtime tests (mutation check, FMBATCH1.md). Dev-proven only.

gate.detail: not a 24h-window requirement: the board's production_window label was inherited from a shared mapping note

F-381.consumer: ops/deploy.sh: readback failure -> ops/rollback_decision.py -> exit 6 + guarded rollback (deploy.sh --rollback-to <predecessor>) on P0, exit 5 fix-forward on P1
F-381.next_action: release: the next deploy through ops/deploy.sh carries the severity rule
evidence: brambleloop/release/DEPLOYED_HISTORY.json: every production commit since fcb982d recorded (b931d17 2026-10-20T03:49Z with pre-deploy backup restore_ok); research/final_build/w4/evidence_ROLLBACK/rehearse_rollback_*.json
F-381.reason: Criterion: 'Every material autonomous deployment preserves a known-good predecessor and an executable rollback/recovery path. Detected regression triggers containment and rollback according to severity.' The predecessor and the executable path were already proven (W4-ROLLBACK). The missing half was severity: a failed readback ended in exit 5 whatever failed. ops/rollback_decision.py classifies readback failures (P0: shadow phase, nothing published, refusals recorded, catalogue unpublished, cost ceilings, boot guard, worker alive, release identity; FAIL or UNKNOWN; production unreachable) and deploy.sh rolls a P0 back to the predecessor through the guarded rollback path, fixes a P1 forward, never rolls back a rollback. Run end to end against a local bare remote. Dev-proven only.

F-380.next_action: release: deploy carrying F-381's severity rule (post-deploy observation proportional to blast radius)
evidence: ops/deploy.sh is the one sanctioned deploy: deploy_guard check (descendant of production + green release-eligible suite record for the exact sha, tracked RELEASE_<sha>.json), rehearse-rollback, push, verify_deploy, per-feature readback (ops/readback.py)
brambleloop/release/DEPLOYED_HISTORY.json b931d17 entry: owner-approved, pre-deploy backup restore_ok, ops/deploy.sh pushed 1b21e81..b931d17, boot_guard record RELEASE_324927f..., readback run
ops/hooks/pre-push routes any push to the production branch through the same guard (tests/test_deploy_path.py)
F-380.reason: Criterion: 'Autonomous code changes require tests, version control, deploy evidence, rollback capability and post-deploy observation appropriate to their blast radius. Production self-modification is never an unversioned live edit.' The matrix next_action (a deploy gate that refuses a deploy unless the suite passed on the sha, then records deploy sha + verify result) exists as ops/deploy.sh + ops/deploy_guard.py and was used for b931d17; production code only changes by a push to the production branch, which the pre-push hook guards. The 'appropriate to blast radius' half lands with F-381 on this branch, so this entry is dev-proven until that release.
